nodes.title: Reorder-buffer overflow during saturation shifts — hard session error instead of backpressure (addressed in S14 WIP)

passages.text: During saturation shifts the reorder buffer could overflow its 4 MiB cap and fail the whole session. S14 WIP: cap raised to 16 MiB and a backpressure path added (ReorderBuffer::would_overflow; the endpoint holds the frame up to REORDER_PAUSE_MAX 5 s — carrier TCP backpressure throttles the sender while the gap drains; soft cap afterwards).

nodes.title: Uneven traffic split under saturation — one adapter maxes out, excess does NOT spill to remaining adapters

passages.text: User-reported (recurring): traffic is not being split evenly; when one adapter reaches its maximum bandwidth range, the rest of the traffic does not split over to the remaining adapters. First addressed by D23/v0.7.0 (balanced pressure + priority ramp-spill) for the per-connection path; the stream-bonding frame scheduler had no saturation signal, so a maxed-out carrier kept receiving frames. S14 fix implemented + gated (peer-reported delivery rates; see task:saturation-aware-split) — awaiting release v0.8.0 and real-setup verification before closing.

- **S2-REV-C: APPROVE** — 0×P0, 1 residual P1 (concurrent external start() in the ~50 ms post-death window; unreachable via Supervisor; one-line hardening suggested), 11×P2. All round-1 findings confirmed fixed (P0-1, P0-2, P1-1, P1-2, P1-3, P2-1). - Full report: agent-reports/s2-rev-c-round2.md - **S2-REV-B: APPROVE** — 0×P0, 1 residual P1 (Winsock does not document nonblocking inheritance for accept()ed sockets → stub could WouldBlock-race on the windows-latest CI leg; test-only), 5×P2 (notices completeness, generate/doctor bypass the loopback guard, disconnect may block ~15 s behind an in-flight connect — documented for S3, lint only covers Linux surface → fixed, process note on the gate incident). nodes.title: D1 — Rust instead of Go (user directive, 2026-11-12)

passages.text: The Go prototype is superseded. All production code is Rust. Design contracts (mux off, loopback inbounds, ordering, fail-open) carry over unchanged.

nodes.title: D10 — vless:// importer is REALITY-only and strict (2026-11-17)

passages.text: MultiTunnel generates exactly one protocol shape (xrayconf: VLESS/TCP/ REALITY/xtls-rprx-vision, chrome fp, spiderX /). `multitunnel import` therefore accepts only links it can faithfully represent: security=reality, type=tcp, flow absent or xtls-rprx-vision; uuid 8-4-4-4-12 hex; pbk exactly 43 unpadded base64url chars; sid empty or 1-16 hex. Unknown query params are ignored (other clients append extras such as headerType, path, alpn, allowInsecure). No percent-decoding of stored fields (uuid/host/port/sni/ pbk/sid never carry escapes; the remark fragment is display-only, not stored). Error messages never echo uuid/pbk values (D9). config.json is patched as RAW JSON — only the server block is replaced — so user-customized ports/paths/behavior survive and relative paths are not re-rooted by a resolve() round-trip. Writes go through write_private (fsutil atomic, S5). Missing config → template first, then patch. (Feature built on a stale-tree session and salvaged onto the frontier after the 7th rollback.)

v0.3 north star: one app, zero user-installed dependencies, v2rayN + net-merge functions out of the box, Material You GUI, Rust core. The user never manually installs an Xray core or net-merge: the engine is located, verified, downloaded (or embedded at build time) by mt-platform; link spreading moves in-process into mt-net. The managed Xray engine remains the REALITY specialist until S7's native port (stock rustls cannot do the REALITY ClientHello auth; a faithful port needs a custom TLS 1.3 stack — tracked, not rushed).

Engine resolution order: $MULTITUNNEL_ENGINE → exe-dir/engine → config-dir/engine (sha256-verified against SHA256SUMS; strict mode refuses mismatch) → build-time embedded zip (MT_EMBED_ENGINE) → explicit user-triggered download (GitHub latest, URL overridable). `locate()` never downloads; only `ensure()` may, and the GUI/CLI surfaces it.

nodes.title: D15 — Bare launch = GUI; a GUI app never dies invisibly (2026-11-18)

passages.text: User report on the v0.3.0 release: "multitunnel.exe does not show a GUI when opened. There does not appear to be any launch activity." Root cause: the no-args default was the `tray` command, which only printed a pointer to the separate multitunnel-tray.exe and exited 1 — a console-subsystem double-click flashes a console for a fraction of a second. The build was never broken; the product's front door was. v0.3.1 rules: 1. Bare launch defaults to `gui` (`command_from`, regression-tested). 2. Windows console policy (`console_mode`): a console-subsystem GUI launch detaches its console via FreeConsole ONLY when the process is the sole console user (GetConsoleProcessList == 1 — Explorer double-click, autostart Run key, `start`); a terminal launch shares the console and keeps it. Call failures conservatively read as "shared" — never detach a console we might share. Side effect: the parked C-P2-10 autostart concern is largely resolved (autostarted console exe now opens the GUI with no lingering console). 3. Never-die-invisibly: GUI launch errors surface as a MessageBoxW when no shared console exists (`alert_error`), and a panic hook (`install_panic_dialog_hook`) shows panics the same way in flash-death processes. stderr remains the primary channel whenever a console survives the process. 4. `gui_args()`: the `gui` dispatch arm must accept an EMPTY argv tail — `&cmd_args[1..]` panicked on the bare launch (a hidden precondition the v0.3.0 `tray` default masked). Caught only by running the host binary bare: unit tests and `gui --smoke` never exercise empty-argv dispatch.

nodes.title: D16 — Adapter bonding via per-adapter engines + Xray `sendThrough` (S8, 2026-11-18)

passages.text: User report: "There is no menu to select the network adapters that are being bonded for the vless connection." Root cause: the merge aggregator, policies and probers existed, but `EngineLinkFactory` built exactly ONE unbound engine — bonding had no adapter surface at all. S8 rules: 1. Enumeration lives in mt-platform (`adapters` module): Windows `GetAdaptersAddresses` FFI (windows-sys, AF_INET, loopback excluded, buffer-retry, 16 MiB cap, fail-open to an empty vec); non-Windows is a pure-std /proc+/sys dev path (IPv4 attribution documented-limited). `NetAdapter.id` = the stable machine id (Windows ANSI AdapterName GUID / Linux ifname) — settings persist IDS, never display names. 2. Binding model: ONE `ManagedEngine` per selected adapter, its Xray config carrying `"sendThrough": <adapter IPv4>` (top-level outbound field; Windows source-address binding selects the egress interface). Engine tags embed the adapter name (`"profile [Wi-Fi]"`, deduplicated) so config/log files never collide; each engine keeps its own ephemeral loopback SOCKS port. Mux stays OFF — the aggregator spreads individual TCP connections across the per-adapter links (net-merge model). 3. Selection is id-validated (`set_bonded_adapters` rejects unknown ids), persisted in `settings.json` (`SettingsView.bonded_adapters`, `#[serde(default)]` so v0.3 files load), and applied on the NEXT connect; a live session is restarted immediately on Apply. Unknown ids or IPv4-less adapters at connect time are SKIPPED with a warning (fail-open — an unplugged USB modem must not black-hole the tunnel). 4.

nodes.title: D17 — Stream bonding protocol (S9, 2026-11-18): mt-bond framing over N REALITY carriers

passages.text: User want: one logical connection, bytes split across the bonded adapters, re-merged at the server; reverse symmetric. Design: 1. TRANSPORT: each adapter keeps its per-adapter engine (D16); a CARRIER is one long-lived connection dialed through one engine whose VLESS target is `127.0.0.1:<merge_port>` ON THE SERVER — server Xray (freedom) pipes it to the `mt-merge-server` daemon. REALITY/vision unchanged per carrier. 2. FRAMING: fixed 24-byte little-endian header (magic 0x4D54, version 1, kind, bond_id u32, session u32, seq u64, len u32) + payload; kinds HELLO/OPEN/DATA/CLOSE/ACK/PING/PONG; DATA ≤ 16 KiB. Carriers are plain byte streams — framing is end-to-end between client bond engine and the daemon, invisible to Xray. 3. RELIABILITY: per-session cumulative ACKs; sender keeps unacked frames; carrier death (write err / EOF / pong timeout) replays unacked frames on live carriers; receiver reorders (drop dupes, buffer gaps, stall-close at 10 s). Backpressure is TCP-native: bounded demux channels → reader blocks → carrier socket buffers fill → sender stalls (no windowing protocol). 4. SCHEDULING: round-robin across live carriers (predictable even split — exactly what the user asked); per-carrier PING RTT EWMA powers health + the Status rows; weighted scheduling is future work. 5. FALLBACK: `bond_mode=stream` with <2 usable carriers → per-connection mode + LogLine (never black-hole). 6. DAEMON: loopback-only (127.0.0.1) — authentication is REALITY+UUID at the Xray edge; no extra secret in v0.5, documented.

nodes.title: D18 — Exit probe: plain HTTP inside the tunnel (S9, 2026-11-18)

passages.text: `exit_probe()` rides the LIVE session: SOCKS CONNECT (through the local listener) to `ip-api.com:80` + hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 GET, parse {query,country,city,isp,as}. Plain HTTP is deliberate: the client→server leg is REALITY-encrypted, and the last hop carries only the echo payload — no TLS stack enters the tree (zero-dep rule). The Status card compares the measured exit against the profile endpoint and calls out mismatches (the GCP-VM-VPN-egress case: exit ISP ≠ Google → server-side egress explanation, NOT a hidden MultiTunnel hop).

nodes.title: D20 — v0.5.1: visibility fixes driven by the first real two-adapter run (S9.1, 2026-11-18)

passages.text: User report on v0.5.0 with Ethernet+Wi-Fi ticked: (1) all traffic rode Ethernet only; (2) the Status graph never appeared; (3) wanted one combined color-coded graph + per-interface graphs under an arrow.

1. GRAPH COORDINATES: iced 0.13's Canvas draws through `renderer.with_translation(bounds.x, bounds.y)` — a Program's frame is in LOCAL space. v0.5.0's RateGraph computed every point from `bounds.x/y`, double-offsetting the plot outside the card (invisible, "graph does not load"). Fix: draw into `Rectangle::new(ORIGIN, bounds.size())`; regression test pins points inside the local rect for a realistically-offset widget rect. Unit tests never caught it because they used origin bounds. LESSON: a canvas program's helpers should never see widget-space coordinates at all. 2. MERGE POLICY DEFAULT: v0.5.0 shipped `merge_policy = "failover"`, and Failover always picks the FIRST healthy link — with Ethernet enumerated first, Wi-Fi stayed idle until Ethernet died. Users read that as broken bonding (it is failover semantics). v0.5.1: default round-robin (connections alternate), unknown-string fallback also round-robin, and a `settings_version` field (default 0 = v0.5.0 file) migrates the STOCK failover value to round-robin on load (best-effort persist). An explicit failover on a version>=1 file is respected verbatim — the migration is once, ever. 3. CARRIER VISIBILITY: ensure_carriers now returns a CarrierReport {live, lines} — one human line per link ("live" / "down (reason)") — and connect_flow emits them as ServiceEvent::LogLine so the GUI log shows per-carrier verdicts; <all-live emits a WARN with the share semantics. 1. VENDORED ICED PATCHES over an iced upgrade: iced_graphics and iced_tiny_skia are at their TERMINAL 0.13.0 releases (no 0.13.x patch line exists), and 0.14/1.0 is a breaking migration. The three defects (local-vs-absolute clip space in damage + render mask; INFINITY marker bounds on canvas text → NaN damage; non-total sort comparator) are fixed as minimal vendored patches under vendor/ with [patch.crates-io], inline comments, per-patch READMEs and regression tests inside the vendored crates (`cargo test -p iced_graphics -p iced_tiny_skia`). LESSON: before upgrading iced wholesale, diff the canvas/damage paths — these fixes must be re-based or dropped deliberately when the dependency moves. 2. CANVAS TEXT BOUNDS are now MEASURED (one no-wrap cosmic-text layout per label per frame, ~µs) instead of INFINITY markers. The anchor stays the alignment position and the size is the measured line — both consumers (visible_bounds for damage, draw_cached for rendering) apply the same alignment arithmetic to the same rectangle. A first attempt that reused the frame clip as conservative bounds BROKE the draw anchor (draw_cached re-anchors via `..bounds`), pushing the right-aligned rate label to the window edge — caught by the Xvfb rig and fixed by measuring instead. 3. EXCLUSIONS SEMANTICS: every plain-list entry imports as action `direct`; v2rayN JSON keeps its own outbound tags where they map (direct/freedom, proxy, block/blackhole).

nodes.title: D23 — S11: even byte spreading (Balanced) + adapter priority order (Priority), v0.7.0

passages.text: User report: with 3+ bonded adapters, one carries most traffic, the second less, the third rarely any. Root cause: round-robin evens CONNECTION COUNT, not BYTES — a single fat flow dominates its adapter. (D22 was the S10.1 HiDPI fix — recorded in the ledger, no separate section here.)

1. BALANCED (new stock default) is load-aware spreading: each new connection goes to the link with the least live pressure (`rate_bps + active_conns × 128 KiB/s`). The per-connection reserve exists specifically so a burst of connections inside one 1 s counter tick spreads instead of stacking on the one link whose byte counters have not ticked yet. Ties rotate via the shared cursor, so an idle table degrades to exactly round-robin. Settings migration v2 moves the stock round-robin to balanced ONCE (D20 precedent: a version<2 file carrying the stock value is indistinguishable from an explicit choice; an explicit re-choice persists). 2. SATURATION IS A PLATEAU, NOT A LEVEL. The learned capacity rises to meet any new rate, so "rate ≈ capacity" is true during a ramp too — a naive threshold would mark a link saturated on its first fat flow. Priority therefore requires the capacity to have STOPPED rising (≥2%/tick resets the streak; the rate EWMA damps jitter below that) for 3+ ticks AND rate ≥ 0.85×capacity AND capacity ≥ 256 KiB/s. Consequences: a still-climbing link is never saturated (priority keeps feeding #1 while it ramps); a pinned link saturates within seconds of plateauing; when demand drops below the band the link un-saturates immediately (priority returns traffic to #1 long before the capacity decays). 3. PRIORITY ORDER = the bonded_adapters LIST ORDER (ids persisted in order since S8; links and stream carriers are built in that order, so link index IS priority).

MOCK FIDELITY: seed_adapters now carries EIGHT adapters (the 3-NIC bond + Bluetooth, vEthernet (WSL), Tailscale, Loopback, VirtualBox — a realistic Windows enumeration); only the 3 wired ones are bonded. This is what exposed the stale test idiom: the toggle test's apply step used to send ALL row ids to set_bonded_adapters (the real AdaptersApply filters to selected rows; the all-bonded 3-seed made the two indistinguishable). Test now mirrors production. 4. ## 2. Findings by severity
### P0 — none
Cross-build is green and proven (imports above); windows-sys feature list covers every referenced API; no license contamination; both CI workflows are functional.

**P1-1. A `v*` tag releases without any test run.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2-4` triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` and PRs — a tag push does **not** trigger ci.yml. `.github/workflows/release.yml:9-14` goes straight to `cargo build --release` with no test/lint step. So the official release artifact can be built from code that never ran the suite (e.g. a tag pushed ahead of a green main commit). Fix: add a `cargo test` step to build-windows (and ideally ubuntu too) in release.yml, or make the release job depend on the ci workflow.

**P1-2. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is referenced by LICENSE and release.yml but does not exist in the tree.** `LICENSE:23-25` states "Third-party components … (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in releases)"; `release.yml:21-23` lists it in the copy loop behind a `Test-Path` guard. The file is absent, so the guard silently drops it and every release zip ships without the notices the project's own LICENSE promises (MIT attribution for winreg, serde/regex/windows-sys dual-license choice, MPL-2.0 statement for the non-redistributed Xray-core). Not contamination (see §3.5), but it should be authored before the first `v*` tag.

**P1-3. `connect()` and `disconnect()` are not serialized — concurrent call can leave a half-up tunnel with `State::Failed`/`Connected` mismatch (S3 landmine).** `supervisor.rs:238-260` (connect), `:264-341` (connect_sequence), `:396-433` (disconnect). If `disconnect()` runs while `connect_sequence()` is in flight (state `Connecting`), the loop handle is still `None` (spawn_loop runs at the *end* of connect), so disconnect joins nothing and immediately restores the proxy / stops the core; connect_sequence then continues through steps 4–5 **after** the disconnect: `net-merge on` and `sysproxy::set` re-run, and either the state ends `Connected` with a live loop that undoes the user's disconnect (spawn_loop resets the stop flag at `:386`), or (restartMax=0) `Failed` with net-merge left on and the proxy restored by the campaign but no owner. Also, the loop's `wait_for_port`/`socks_probe` (up to 15 s each) are not stop-flag-aware, so disconnect can block a calling thread ~15 s. Unreachable from the S2 CLI (main.rs: `connect()?` then sleep-forever, single thread), but the module contract (`supervisor.rs:29-31`) explicitly hands the S3 tray an `Arc<Supervisor>` callable "from menu handlers on any thread" — a quick connect→disconnect click sequence is exactly that. Fix before S3: one cycle mutex / in-flight guard around connect+disconnect, and make the loop's port-wait/probe stoppable.

**P2-1. Unused windows-sys feature.** `Cargo.toml:27` enables `Win32_System_LibraryLoader`, but no code references `GetModuleHandle`/`LoadLibrary` (grep over src: zero hits). Harmless (declaration-only crate) but it is dead dependency surface — drop it.

**P2-2. CI never enforces the project's own fmt/clippy gates.** `ci.yml` runs only `cargo test` + zigbuild. The harness treats "clippy clean / fmt clean" as gate criteria; a regression in either lands silently. Add a lint job (`cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`).

**P2-3. `core_proc.rs` test stub still uses the blocking-accept pattern that caused the supervisor hang.** `core_proc.rs:421-444` (`stub_socks`: blocking `listener.accept().expect(...)`, `:454` join). It is provably unhangable here — the probe always connects before anything can fail (addr comes from the bound listener) and the stub thread ends right after writing its reply, independent of the probe — but supervisor's stub was hardened (nonblocking accept + quit flag, `supervisor.rs:705-754`) precisely because this *class* of bug hung the suite once. Apply the same pattern for defense-in-depth.

**P2-4. Narrow `spawn_loop` race after a give-up.** `supervisor.rs:377-392` vs `:497`. ## P0 — must fix before close
### P0-1 — `CoreProc::start()` hangs (and then double-starts) when a child is already running **`src/core_proc.rs:108-116`** (doc claim at `:104`, module doc `:10-11`)
`start()` joins the previous waiter thread **before** checking the child slot:

The waiter (`waiter_loop`, :333-367) only exits when the child dies, the slot empties, or the stop flag is set. So while a child is live, `join()` blocks **indefinitely**; the `is_some()` error branch is dead code on that path. When the child eventually dies, the join returns, the (now empty) slot passes the check, and `start()` spawns a *new* child and returns `Ok(())` — a silent double-generation restart the caller never asked for. This violates the method's own contract ("Returns an error if a child is already running") and is an unbounded block in a public lib API that stage S3 (tray) is specified to call from menu threads.

Reachability inside the supervisor today is via P0-2's corrupted states (e.g. `State::Failed` with a live core → next `connect()` → `connect_sequence` step 2 → `core.start()` → wedged forever); it is also directly reachable by any external API user. **Fix (trivial):** check `lock(&self.child).is_some()` and return the error *before* joining the leftover waiter (the leftover join is only safe when the previous cycle's child is gone).

### P0-2 — `connect()` and `disconnect()` are not serialized as whole operations; disconnect can be silently ineffective **`src/supervisor.rs:238-260` (connect), `:264-341` (connect_sequence), `:396-433` (disconnect)**

Only the tiny state-check windows hold `inner`. `connect_sequence` performs seconds of work (config write, core spawn, up-to-15 s port wait, up-to-20 s probe, up-to-15 s bonding wait) holding **no lock and no joinable loop handle** — `spawn_loop` runs only *after* it succeeds. A concurrent `disconnect()` sees `state != Disconnected`, sets the stop flag, joins a **`None`** loop handle (`:402` — the loop doesn't exist yet), restores proxy, stops whatever core exists, sets `Disconnected`, and returns `Ok` — while `connect_sequence` keeps running. Demonstrated (44 ms disconnect during an in-flight probe): final state `Connected`, poll loop alive; with `restart_max > 0` the loop even resurrects the core the disconnect killed, and step 5 sets the **system proxy after the user disconnected**, which in the kill-window black-holes all WinINET traffic through a dead proxy.

This is exactly the usage the module docs advertise for S3 ("wrap the `Supervisor` in an `Arc` and call from menu handlers on any thread", :29-31). It also compounds with P0-1: the interleaving `connect A → disconnect B (completes early) → connect C` can leave `State::Failed`/`Disconnected` with a live core, after which the next `connect()` blocks forever in `start()`'s waiter join. **Fix:** one operation-level `Mutex<()>` (or making the state transition a token) held for the whole of `connect()`/`disconnect()`; all methods are already `&self`, so this is local and cheap.
## P1 — should fix
### P1-1 — `socks_probe` has per-read timeouts but no total deadline **`src/core_proc.rs:259-268, 390-393`**

`set_read_timeout(timeout)` bounds each `read_exact`, but a proxy that drips one byte just inside every timeout window keeps each read alive forever — the probe never returns. The contract ("a probe against a malicious/half-open proxy must never hang", module doc :14-16) is satisfied per-read, not per-call. Consequences: `connect()` blocks unboundedly at step 3; the poll loop stalls mid-probe (no tick, no stop-flag observation), and since `disconnect()` joins the loop thread, a tray disconnect wedges with it. Practical exposure is low (the probed proxy is our own spawned xray on loopback), hence P1 not P0. **Fix:** compute a call deadline and re-set `read_timeout` to the remaining budget before each read.

### P1-2 — `elevate::join_args` does not escape quotes / backslash-before-quote (argument injection into the elevated relaunch) **`src/elevate.rs:17-28`** (used at `src/main.rs:314` via `relaunch_elevated`)

Arguments containing whitespace are wrapped in quotes but embedded `"` is never escaped. An argument like `a" --evil` becomes `"a" --evil"`, which `CommandLineToArgvW` parses as **two** arguments (`a`, `--evil"`) — a single crafted argv entry splits into multiple arguments in the UAC-elevated child. Similarly a path argument ending in `\` (e.g. `-config C:\`) corrupts: `"C:\"` parses as `C:"`. Today's exposure is same-user self-injection (the user launches the CLI), but `main.rs` forwards arbitrary `std::env::args()` verbatim, so any future caller that passes semi-trusted arguments turns this into a real elevation-boundary injection. **Fix:** proper `CommandLineToArgvW`-compatible escaping (`"` → `\"`, doubling trailing backslashes before a closing quote).

### P1-3 — cross-module: `local.listen` is never validated to be loopback (contract #2) **`src/config.rs:234-263` (validate), `src/xrayconf.rs:20,27` (binds verbatim), `src/supervisor.rs:609-616` (socks_addr/http_addr)**

`Config::validate` checks server fields and port collision only. A config with `"listen": "0.0.0.0"` passes validation, is bound verbatim by **both** xray inbounds — the SOCKS inbound is `"auth": "noauth"` (`xrayconf.rs:23`) — exposing an unauthenticated SOCKS+HTTP proxy to the LAN, and becomes the WinINET `ProxyServer` value. This directly violates the lib.rs architecture contract #2 ("the core exposes loopback-only SOCKS/HTTP inbounds"). Defaults are safe (`127.0.0.1`) and `doctor` only checks parseability (`main.rs:237`), so it is a config-reachable footgun rather than an exploit — but the S2 supervisor is the natural enforcement point (fail `connect_sequence` if `socks_addr`/`http_addr` is not loopback), or add the check to `Config::validate` in a follow-up. Flagged as a cross-module contract violation per stage instructions (config.rs is S1-closed).

### P0-1 — `CoreProc::start()` waiter-join hang — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/core_proc.rs:105-124`: the child-slot check is now FIRST (`:109-111`) and returns the documented `Err`; the leftover-waiter join (`:115-117`) runs only when the slot is empty; a re-check under the slot lock (`:119-124`) covers the join window. Verified:

- **Soundness of the join:** with the slot empty, the old waiter has either exited or will observe `None` within one 50 ms poll (`waiter_loop`, :346-380) — the join is bounded. The re-check under the slot lock closes the TOCTOU between first check and join completion. - **Concurrent `start()`×2:** the slot lock is held across the whole spawn+publish region (`:119-198`), so a loser blocks at its first check and then sees `Some` → Err. No double-spawn. - **The orchestrator's question (child dies between check and join):** if a child is alive at the first check → immediate Err (no join). If the slot is empty, the join cannot wait on a live child — the waiter's exit conditions don't depend on any child. ✓ - Empirical demo + new test `start_while_running_errors_promptly` (`<1 s` bound on an instant Err — µs in practice, huge margin). ✓ - **Residual (new P1-1 below):** a theoretical hang remains for *concurrent external* `start()` calls hitting the ~50 ms window where the old waiter hasn't exited yet and another `start()` publishes a fresh child the old waiter then adopts. Not reachable through `Supervisor` (see op_lock analysis), so P1 hardening, not P0.

### P0-2 — connect/disconnect not serialized — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/supervisor.rs:178,209,247-248,413-414`: `Shared::op_lock: Mutex<()>` acquired for the **whole body** of `connect()` and `disconnect()`; poison-tolerant `lock()`; guard released by RAII on every path. Verified by demo (above) and by `connect_waits_for_op_lock_of_in_flight_operation` (a blocked connect cannot even set `Connecting`). **Deadlock analysis (the specific question):**

- `op_lock` is taken **only** by `connect()`/`disconnect()` (grep: :248, :414 + test) — the poll loop, restart campaign, and all helpers never take it. `disconnect()` joining the loop while holding op_lock therefore cannot deadlock; worst case it waits out one bounded blocking call (see below). - Lock nesting is strictly one-way: op_lock → {inner, loop_thread, core locks}, never the reverse; every inner/loop_thread acquisition is a standalone short statement. No ABBA cycle. - `spawn_loop` (`:391-408`) drops the loop_thread guard **before** joining and re-acquires after — and both `spawn_loop` and `disconnect` (the only slot writers) run under op_lock, so the re-acquire window is race-free. The old `loop_running` early-return (REV-B P2-4) is gone; the join target is provably exited: the only paths leaving a handle in the slot are give-up (loop already returned — `loop_running=false` is its final statement) or a just-exiting give-up thread (ns window). A *live* loop implies state Connecting/Connected, for which `connect()` no-ops before `spawn_loop` — so joining a live loop is unreachable. - Loop-join blocking is bounded: ticks sleep in 100 ms stoppable slices, campaigns re-check the stop flag every iteration, `wait_for_port` ≤ 15 s, `socks_probe` now has a **total** deadline (P1-1 fix), netmerge calls have hard timeouts. So `disconnect()` holds op_lock at most ~15-30 s; a concurrent connect waits, then sees the settled state. Serialization latency, not a hang — and it is exactly what makes the round-1 race impossible.

### P1-1 — `socks_probe` total deadline — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/core_proc.rs:271-277, 402-440`. The design is correct this time and the reasoning in the fix note is right: socket timeouts are per-underlying-syscall, so the budget must be re-armed before **every** `read` call, not per logical read. Verified in detail:

- `refresh_socket_budget` (:404-420): `checked_duration_since` (None → Err) + explicit `is_zero` guard, then sets BOTH read and write timeouts to the remaining budget. No panic; errors are `socks5:`-prefixed. - `socks_read_exact` (:427-…): manual fill loop — re-arms the budget before each `s.read`, `Ok(0)` → clean "connection closed" error, io errors (incl. `TimedOut`/`WouldBlock` from the shrunken window) propagate with context, `filled` arithmetic cannot exceed `buf.len()` (read contract), empty buffer → no-op Ok. **No panic surface.** - Every reply phase (greeting, head, ATYP length, drain) passes the same deadline; the CONNECT write is preceded by its own refresh (:304). Total probe time ≤ `timeout` + ε for any drip schedule: each read's timeout is the *remaining* budget, so the deadline is a hard ceiling. - The new test drips 12 valid SOCKS5 reply bytes at 80 ms intervals against a 500 ms budget and asserts Err in **[350, 900) ms**. Timing analysis on a loaded 2-core box: in *every* delivery schedule the probe errors at ~500 ms (a delayed drip merely moves the failing read to the deadline; an on-time drip completes the head at ~480 ms and the drain read then has ~20 ms left), so the window has ≥150 ms lower / ≥400 ms upper margin — the tightest test in the suite but sound; observed stable across my 4 runs. Without the fix the probe returns Ok at ~880 ms and the test fails on `expect_err` — it genuinely pins the bug.

### P1-2 — argv quoting — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/elevate.rs:35-77`: `quote_windows_arg` implements the full `CommandLineToArgvW` rules. Verified against the rules case by case: n backslashes before a quote → `2n+1` (parses back as n literal backslashes + non-toggling quote) ✓; backslashes before any other char → literal ✓; trailing backslashes doubled before the closing quote ✓; bare args (no whitespace/quote, non-empty) untouched — so bare `C:\` round-trips without the trailing-backslash trap ✓; empty → `""` ✓; quote-only arg `"` → `"\""` ✓. The round-1 injection case `a" --evil` now produces `"a\" --evil"` → re-parses to the **single** original argument (tested). `join_args` keeps the space separator. Tests cover `a" --evil`, `C:\my dir\`, bare `C:\`, `a\b"c`, plain `a\b`. Correct.

### P1-3 — loopback enforcement — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/supervisor.rs:279-281, 616-634`: `ensure_loopback_listen` runs at connect step 0.5 — after the stale-proxy self-heal, **before** any config write or core spawn, so a bad `listen` fails fast into `State::Failed` with a clear message. Correctness: `"localhost"` allowed (ASCII case-insensitive), IP parse → `IpAddr::is_loopback()` — which covers the whole `127.0.0.0/8` (`127.9.9.9` ✓) and `::1` ✓; `0.0.0.0`, `::`, private/link-local IPs, garbage and empty strings are all rejected with `local.listen`-named errors (tested exhaustively). Non-IP strings like `192.168.1.5:1080` (bad config shapes) are rejected rather than guessed ✓. Note: `restart_campaign` doesn't re-check, but the config is immutable per Supervisor and connect_sequence validated it before the loop can exist — sound. Config.rs untouched as agreed (S1-closed).

**Windows implementation** (`mod win`, all FFI through windows-sys 0.61.2, **no new Cargo features** — only the already-enabled Win32_Foundation/Win32_UI_Shell/Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging):

- **Window**: `CreateWindowExW` with the predefined `"STATIC"` system class, `HWND_MESSAGE` parent, style 0 (message-only, never shown) — no RegisterClass. ## Key FFI decisions (for the unsafe reviewer)

1. **RT_ICON bytes, not the file**: `CreateIconFromResourceEx` requires the image bytes an ICONDIRENTRY points at; passing the whole ICO file is the classic mistake. `ico_image_bytes` extracts+bounds-checks the slice; a unit test pins the 32×32 entry's header (biSize=40/biWidth=32/biHeight=64). 2. **STATIC + GWLP_WNDPROC subclass** instead of RegisterClass (fewer moving parts, per the stage spec). The previous proc pointer is checked non-null; we intentionally call `DefWindowProcW` (not `CallWindowProcW` on the saved STATIC proc) for unhandled messages — a message-only window never uses static-control behavior after creation. 3. **No GWLP_USERDATA**: state flows through a thread-local `&'static` (single window, single message thread). Every one of the 32 `unsafe` blocks carries a `SAFETY:` comment; error paths use `std::io::Error::last_os_error()` (thread-safe errno) rather than raw `GetLastError`.

### 2.2 windows-sys feature list vs APIs used (item 8) mod win references: Foundation `{HWND, LPARAM, LRESULT, POINT, WPARAM}`; UI::Shell `{Shell_NotifyIconW, NOTIFYICONDATAW, NIF_*, NIM_*}`; UI::WindowsAndMessaging `{AppendMenuW, CreateIconFromResourceEx, CreatePopupMenu, CreateWindowExW, DefWindowProcW, DestroyIcon, DestroyMenu, DestroyWindow, DispatchMessageW, GetCursorPos, GetMessageW, KillTimer, LoadIconW, PostMessageW, PostQuitMessage, SetForegroundWindow, SetTimer, SetWindowLongPtrW, TrackPopupMenuEx, TranslateMessage, GWLP_WNDPROC, HICON, HMENU, HWND_MESSAGE, IDI_APPLICATION, LR_DEFAULTCOLOR, MF_*, MSG, TPM_*, WM_*}`. All inside the three already-enabled features (Win32_Foundation, Win32_UI_Shell, Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging) — **no new features needed, none added**. `CreateIconFromResourceEx`'s windows-sys 0.61.2 signature matches the call site (verified by the target clippy + link; the crate declares the same mapping for gnu and MSVC, so the windows-latest MSVC leg compiles identically — windows-sys has no target-specific declarations for these). `SetWindowLongPtrW` exists only on 64-bit targets — fine, the project targets x86_64 only. `HWND_MESSAGE`, `IDI_APPLICATION` (PCWSTR), `WM_APP` all resolve. The `-D warnings` cross clippy is the machine proof; the PE import list is the link proof.

### 2.3 GUI-subsystem discipline (item 9) Grep over src: every `println!`/`eprintln!` lives in main.rs (the console binary) or in test code. The tray paths use only `let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr(), …)` (bin main + `log_err`) — the S2-verified non-panicking form. Error/first-run flows are file-based: template + `config-needed.txt` beside the exe (verified by running the host binary). `spawn_detached` targets GUI apps (notepad.exe, explorer.exe) so no console flash even from the GUI-subsystem process. Clean.

### 2.4 Custom build tooling — icon (item 6) - **Deterministic**: stdlib-only (`os/struct/sys`), no RNG, no timestamps, no environment dependence; accepts an output path, so I regenerated to /tmp: `cmp` reports the committed 5430-byte `assets/icon.ico` **byte-identical** to regeneration. - **Format validity** (independent python parse + `file`): ICONDIR reserved=0/type=1/count=2; entries 32×32 (offset 38, 4264 B) and 16×16 (offset 4302, 1128 B); each payload is a BITMAPINFOHEADER with biSize=40, biWidth=n, biHeight=2n (XOR+AND doubled), planes=1, 32 bpp, BI_RGB, and biSizeImage == 40 + n²·4 + padded-AND — exactly the RT_ICON shape `CreateIconFromResourceEx` consumes; XOR rows bottom-up BGRA; corners fully transparent (AND bit set), center navy (42,27,13,255); file ends exactly at the last image (no trailing bytes). `file(1)`: "MS Windows icon resource - 2 icons, 32x32, 32 bits/pixel, 16x16, 32 bits/pixel". - **No emoji**: the only non-ASCII bytes in make_icon.py are em-dashes (U+2014) in comments — punctuation, consistent with repo style; the motif is pure geometry (navy rounded square + two link bars), no text/emoji. - The Rust side pins the 32×32 DIB header in a unit test (biSize=40/biWidth=32/biHeight=64).

### 2.5 Licensing (item 7) Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock **byte-identical to S2-close** — zero new dependencies, so the S2 notices file remains accurate. The icon is original work generated by the project's own committed script (pure geometry, no third-party artwork) → covered by the project MIT license; scripts/make_icon.py is project source. No copyleft, no contamination. My S2 round-2 follow-ups (serde_core row + full MIT text, windows-target clippy in cross-check, `set_nonblocking(false)` in the core_proc stub) verified present at fe613ab.

### 2.6 Test quality (item 10) 20 new tests, all host-runnable against the pure helpers: state labels (all 4 states), links line (3 modes + 0-link edge), tooltip (clean / error+bond+probe / first-line cap at 48 / blank-skip), tip_array (NUL termination, 127-unit cap with slot-127 reserved, surrogate-pair boundary at unit 126, intact pair), ICO (embedded asset parse + DIB header asserts, preference order exact→fits→largest, rejection: empty/truncated/cursor-type/reserved/count-mismatch/len-0/out-of-bounds), status dump (content, placeholder, create-dirs + overwrite semantics), menu (enablement matrix across 4 states, 11-row structure with separators and labels, links line per config), cmd id roundtrip incl. 0/999/0xFFFF. None `#[ignore]`d (run reports 0 ignored); none vacuous — every one asserts exact strings/indices/bytes. Deterministic: no sleeps, clocks, sockets, or processes; the file-based dump test uses the pid+counter unique-dir pattern. 5/5 single-threaded runs at 0.00 s. All Windows-leg-safe (temp dirs + file IO only). One hygiene nit → P2-1.

### 2.7 CI sanity - ci.yml test leg (windows-latest, MSVC) compiles the tray module: same windows-sys crate and feature set proven to compile on windows-gnu; no MSVC-vs-mingw declaration divergence for these APIs. - lint job (host clippy -D warnings) and cross-check (zigbuild + windows-gnu clippy -D warnings, added at S2-close) both cover the new module and pass locally on the exact commands. - release.yml already packages `multitunnel-tray.exe`; the icon is embedded via `include_bytes!`, so the release zip has no runtime asset dependency. No workflow changes needed for S3 — and none were made.
## 3. Findings by severity

### P0 — none Cross-build green and machine-proven (target clippy -D warnings + zigbuild + PE imports); no new dependencies; no license change; CI workflows cover the new code on all three legs (host test, windows test, cross lint+build).

**P1-1. Menu-dismiss pattern on a message-only window is runtime-unverifiable from this sandbox (tray.rs `show_menu`, :839-886).** The KB Q135788 fix calls `SetForegroundWindow(hwnd)` before `TrackPopupMenuEx` (return value discarded) so the menu dismisses when the user clicks elsewhere. `hwnd` is a **message-only** window (child of `HWND_MESSAGE`, style 0, never shown). Activation is a top-level-window concept; if `SetForegroundWindow` is a no-op for a message-only child (plausible per its docs — the call activates the window and brings its thread to the foreground), the classic stuck-menu bug returns despite the pattern being present. Nobody has run this tray on real Windows yet, and it cannot be exercised from Linux. Not build/CI-breaking and not UB — but it should be smoke-tested on real Windows before the first release, or the window created as a **hidden top-level** window (no `HWND_MESSAGE` parent, never shown — the pattern .NET NotifyIcon and the tray-icon crate use), which also keeps `Shell_NotifyIconW` callbacks working. Cross-lens flag for the unsafe reviewer to confirm.

**P2-1. Temp-dir leak in one new test.** `write_status_dump_creates_dirs_and_overwrites` (tray.rs:1249-1263) never `remove_dir_all`s its unique dir — the only test in the crate that doesn't clean up after itself (the S1/S2 review criterion). One line fixes it.

**P2-2. Exit's 2 s disconnect bound gives up on a legitimate ~15 s teardown.** `exit_app` (EXIT_WAIT=2 s) races the supervisor op_lock/poll-loop join that can legally take up to ~15 s; on timeout the process exits mid-disconnect, potentially leaving the system proxy set and net-merge on until the next launch (step-0 self-heal covers it, and the bound is a deliberate anti-hang). Documented trade-off — consider a brief "shutting down…" tooltip update or a slightly larger bound; behavior is safe, just occasionally untidy.

**P2-3. Embedded-asset test under-pins the icon.** `ico_embedded_asset_parses_with_32_entry` asserts the 32×32 DIB header only; a drifted or hand-edited icon.ico would still pass. Cheap hardening: also assert the 16×16 DIB header and the total file length (5430) so any divergence from make_icon.py's deterministic output is caught (a full byte-compare needs python and can't live in cargo test).

**P2-4. `spawn_detached` silently drops spawn failures** (`let _ = Command::…spawn()`) for notepad/explorer — both are inbox Windows components, so this is a nit; a `log_err` on failure would make a missing-shell case diagnosable.
## 4. Verdict

**APPROVE** — 0 P0. All mandatory gates pass on my own runs (77/77 ×5 incl. full-load, 37/37 subset ×3 single-threaded, 20/20 tray ×5, host + windows-gnu clippy `-D warnings` clean, fmt clean, zigbuild green, both PEs with correct subsystems, tray FFI proven linked via import table). No new dependencies, no licensing change, deterministic committed tooling with a byte-identical regeneration, and 20 genuinely assertive host-runnable tests. The single P1 is a runtime smoke-test recommendation (message-only window + SetForegroundWindow) that should be resolved on real Windows before the first release — it does not affect the build, CI, or any host-verifiable behavior.

passages.text: # S3 Review — Reviewer-C (Correctness & Security; special FFI mandate)

- **Reviewer:** Reviewer-C, adversarial round, stage S3 - **Date:** 2026-11-13, repo HEAD `81c7e72` (S3 landed in `0fb81f0` on base `fe613ab`), branch main, clean tree — no files modified; only this report written. - **Scope:** line-by-line audit of every `unsafe` block in `src/tray.rs` (+ `src/bin/tray.rs`, `assets/icon.ico`, `scripts/make_icon.py`, lib.rs diff) against the special S3 mandate: FFI correctness, memory/pointer safety, wndproc re-entrancy, races, GDI/user-handle leaks, panic paths in message handlers, Supervisor-lifecycle interaction.
## Verification log (run myself, trusted nothing)

| Gate | Result | |---|---| | `cargo test` | **77/77 passed, 0 failed** in 6.05 s (20 new tray tests included) | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` (host) | **clean** — 0 warnings | | `cargo clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` | **clean** — exit 0 (denies warnings on the actual FFI target) | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **success** — `multitunnel-tray.exe` = **PE32+ GUI subsystem x86-64** (14 sections), console bin unaffected | | `git show 0fb81f0 --stat` | 6 files: `src/tray.rs` (1353), `src/bin/tray.rs` (106), `assets/icon.ico` (5430 B), `scripts/make_icon.py`, `s3-implementation.md`, lib.rs (+2 doc/module lines only — S1/S2 modules untouched) | | Icon asset byte-level parse (my own Python walk) | 2 entries: 32×32 @ off 38 len 4264, 16×16 @ off 4302 len 1128; payload math exact (40 + w·h·4 + padded AND-mask = declared len for both); no overlap; file ends exactly at 5430. Directory + DIB headers match the Rust unit-test assertions | | windows-sys 0.61.2 source inspection (vendored crate) | `WNDPROC = Option<unsafe extern "system" fn(HWND, u32, WPARAM, LPARAM) -> LRESULT>` — matches `tray_wndproc`; `CreateIconFromResourceEx(*const u8, u32, BOOL, u32, i32, i32, IMAGE_FLAGS) -> HICON` — matches call; `NOTIFYICONDATAW` on x86_64 is `#[repr(C)]` with `szTip: [u16; 128]` (W variant, unicode) — matches `tip_array`'s `[u16;128]`; `SetTimer(HWND, usize, u32, TIMERPROC)`, `TrackPopupMenuEx(HMENU, u32, i32, i32, HWND, *const TPMPARAMS)`, `Shell_NotifyIconW(NOTIFY_ICON_MESSAGE, *const NOTIFYICONDATAW)` — all match.
## Unsafe-block audit — 32 blocks, 32 OK

The wndproc itself (`tray_wndproc`, :675, `unsafe extern "system" fn`) is audited separately below; every `unsafe { … }` block carries a `SAFETY:` comment (32/32), and each comment's claim was checked, not just its presence.

| # | Line | API | Verdict & reasoning | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | :482 | `DestroyIcon` | OK — only when `icon_owned` (from `CreateIconFromResourceEx`) and non-null; nothing references it (no tray icon was added on this failure path) | | 2 | :493 | `DestroyWindow` | OK — window created by this thread on this path; no icon registered | | 3 | :496 | `DestroyIcon` | OK — same guard as #1 on the NIM_ADD-failure path | | 4 | :508 | `SetTimer` | OK — valid hwnd, fresh id 1, `None` TIMERPROC ⇒ WM_TIMER to the subclassed proc; failure (returns 0) is non-fatal and logged | | 5 | :523 | `GetMessageW` | OK — `&mut msg` is a valid aligned `MSG` out-slot; NULL hwnd filter; both i32 outcomes (0 = WM_QUIT, −1 = error → teardown + Err) handled | | 6 | :535 | `TranslateMessage` | OK — `msg` holds a message returned by #5 | | 7 | :537 | `DispatchMessageW` | OK — same; routes to our subclass; wndproc is panic-free (see below) | | 8 | :559 | `Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_DELETE)` (teardown) | OK — identity fields (cbSize/hWnd/uID) set via `nid_base`; guarded by `icon_added` (swap ⇒ idempotent with exit_app's delete); FALSE (already gone) ignored | | 9 | :564 | `KillTimer` | OK — our timer/hwnd; idempotent; ordered before DestroyWindow | | 10 | :566 | `DestroyWindow` (teardown) | OK — our message-only window; the defensive WM_DESTROY handler posts one extra (harmless, never-consumed) WM_QUIT | | 11 | :571 | `DestroyIcon` (teardown) | OK — only when owned; the `LoadIconW` fallback is a SHARED icon and is correctly never destroyed (`icon_owned=false`) — no GDI leak, no shared-icon UAF | | 12 | :587 |

**Wndproc panic-freedom (panic across `extern "system"` = abort/UB):** `tray_wndproc` and everything it calls were walked exhaustively: no indexing, slicing, `unwrap`, `expect`, or arithmetic that hostile data can reach (grep-confirmed zero in `mod win`). The two remaining panic-capable constructs are both proven unreachable: (a) `ctx()`'s `RefCell::borrow` — the CTX cell is mutably borrowed exactly once, before the window exists and before any message dispatch, on the same thread; (b) `ui.borrow_mut()` in `on_timer`/`exit_app`/`teardown` — never held across any message-pumping call (`show_menu` never touches `ui`; the exit wait blocks rather than pumps). Supervisor `snapshot()`/locks use the poison-tolerant `lock()` and are contention-brief (workers hold `inner` only momentarily). Interior NULs in net-merge-sourced tooltip text merely truncate display (fixed-size NUL-terminated buffer), no memory-safety impact.

**Threading / op_lock interaction (mandate item 2):** verified — `connect`/`disconnect` run ONLY via `spawn_supervisor_op` workers; nothing in the wndproc or `show_menu` ever calls a supervisor op synchronously. `exit_app`: NIM_DELETE → worker `disconnect()` → `recv_timeout(2 s)` → PostQuitMessage. No deadlock is possible: the message thread holds no lock the worker needs; op_lock holders never wait on the message thread (verified all op paths: spawn_loop/net-merge/registry/core — none send messages to the window). The orphaned-worker-at-exit scenario is bounded and implicitly documented — but its teardown-completion gap is P1-1 below.

**ICO byte-level bounds (mandate item 1):** `ico_entries`/`ico_image_bytes` re-audited line-by-line: `len < 6` reject, reserved/type magic check, per-entry `checked_add(16)` + `end > len` reject, `dim` from directory byte (0 ⇒ 256), `len == 0` reject, `offset.checked_add(len)` then `slice::get` (no panic on any malformed input; no unwrap). The committed asset itself parses byte-perfect (my independent Python walk). `include_bytes!` is a compile-time embed — no runtime path dependency, stable in release builds.

**Supervisor integration (mandate item 5):** menu enablement matches the state machine exactly (Connect: Disconnected/Failed; Disconnect: Connecting/Connected — cancelling an in-flight connect via op_lock, per the S2 contract; snapshot-staleness between menu open and click is harmless because the supervisor state gate arbitrates). Tooltip surfacing `snapshot.error` (implementer's documented deviation) is correct and I endorse it — without it a Failed state would show no reason. The status dump contains no secrets (snapshot fields + net-merge text; no credentials in any supervisor error string — verified in S2). 1 s timer → `NIM_MODIFY` only on text change — no shell churn.

**Bin cross-check (mandate item 6):** elevation flow forwards original args (`-config` survives; quoting hardened in S2); GUI-subsystem stderr writes are all best-effort `writeln!` with ignored errors — **no `eprintln!` panic-on-invalid-handle anywhere**; the missing-config path is file-based (template + `config-needed.txt` beside the exe — visible without a console); config search order (explicit → beside exe → cwd) and template placement logic verified correct.
## Findings

### P0 — none I could not construct any UB, handle leak, deadlock, or reachable panic in the shipped paths. The three highest-risk patterns (wndproc + RefCell + panic-across-FFI; SetWindowLongPtrW subclass; NOTIFYICONDATAW ABI) are all sound by construction and verified against the actual windows-sys 0.61.2 definitions.

### P1 — 2 1. **`src/tray.rs:807-832` (`exit_app`)** — the 2 s exit budget can be exceeded by a *healthy* disconnect: `disconnect()` joins the poll loop, which may legitimately sit inside `socks_probe` (15 s total budget), a restart campaign's `wait_for_port` (15 s), or `netmerge::off`'s CLI timeout (10 s) — or an in-flight `connect` worker may still hold the op_lock (up to ~50 s). When the 2 s expires, the process exits with teardown incomplete: the xray core is **orphaned** (Windows does not kill children on parent exit) and the system proxy stays set — the user believes the app (and tunnel) exited, while traffic keeps flowing through the VM, or browsing is silently routed through a half-dead proxy. Fix suggestion: on timeout, perform an op_lock-free emergency stop — `CoreProc::stop` (own mutexes, no op_lock) plus `sysproxy::restore(state_dir)` — both safe to call from the message thread; or escalate the wait with a visible "disconnecting…" state. At minimum the incomplete-teardown possibility must be documented as more than "best-effort". 2. **`src/tray.rs` (whole module — no `TaskbarCreated` handling)** — if explorer.exe restarts (shell crash, user-initiated restart — not rare), the tray icon is silently lost and never re-added: the process becomes an elevated, unreachable zombie holding the tunnel with no UI and no window (message-only ⇒ not findable); the only exit is Task Manager. Standard fix: `RegisterWindowMessageW("TaskbarCreated")` handled in the wndproc → re-`NIM_ADD` (icon handle and window survive explorer restarts).

### P2 — 7 1. `src/bin/tray.rs:28,41` + `src/tray.rs:491` — GUI-subsystem errors are invisible: a declined UAC prompt, `NIM_ADD` failure, or any `tray::run` error goes to a best-effort stderr that usually doesn't exist — the user sees nothing happen. Safe (no panic) but a `MessageBoxW` (or writing an error file like the config-note pattern) would make failures diagnosable. 2. `src/tray.rs:797-799` — "Edit config"/"Show raw status" spawn **notepad running elevated**; an elevated editor is the classic admin-shell footgun (its file dialogs can launch arbitrary executables with admin rights). User-initiated and the whole app is elevated by requirement, but worth documenting or delegating to an unelevated broker in a future stage. 3. `src/tray.rs:776-794` — `show_raw_status`/`open_log_folder` do synchronous file writes + `create_dir_all` inside the wndproc (small, but a state dir on slow/network storage would stall the pump); the connect/disconnect worker pattern is the right home for these too. 4. `src/tray.rs:79-87` — `snippet(s, cap)` underflows (`cap - 1`) if ever called with `cap == 0`; unreachable today (sole call site uses 48) but it is a latent panic-in-wndproc if reused — guard or `debug_assert!(cap > 0)`. 5. `src/tray.rs:456` — the "call exactly once" contract for `run` is unenforced; a second call would leak another ctx and create a second window. A cheap `debug_assert`/atomic once-flag would pin the invariant. 6.

### Positive notes - The RT_ICON-not-the-file insight (#12), the surrogate-pair-safe `tip_array`, the no-GWLP_USERDATA thread-local design, the Q135788 dance, the `icon_owned` shared-vs-owned distinction, and the idempotent teardown with swap-guarded `icon_added` are all exactly right — this is a carefully done raw-FFI tray. - The pure-helper/test split (316 pure lines host-tested) is the same pattern that made S1/S2 reviewable, and the 20 new tests genuinely pin the helpers (tip boundary at unit 126, ICO preference order and rejections, menu enablement per state, id round-trip, dump overwrite). - The icon asset is byte-perfect and exactly the size the format dictates (5430 B); `make_icon.py` is deterministic and dev-only (not shipped).
## Verdict

**APPROVE.** No P0: all 32 unsafe blocks are correct with accurate SAFETY comments (signatures and struct layouts verified against the vendored windows-sys 0.61.2 source, not assumed); the wndproc is provably panic-free; no GDI/user-handle leaks on any path; no deadlock in the op_lock interaction; all four mandatory gates green. The two P1s (exit-teardown completeness, TaskbarCreated re-add) are production-readiness items that should be fixed before the S4 release but do not introduce UB, leaks, deadlocks, or reachable panics; P2-7 needs one on-hardware check during S4 smoke testing.
*Repo untouched (clean tree at `81c7e72`); the only write is this report.*

passages.text: # S4 Implementation — Server script + README + QUICKSTART

- **Implementer:** S4 agent (implementation round, stage S4) - **Date:** 2026-11-13, repo base 06ad6aa (S3 closed), branch main - **Scope:** three new files only — `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` (new `server/` dir, chmod +x), `README.md`, `QUICKSTART.md`. No change to `src/`, `.github/`, `Cargo.*`, `config.example.json`, or any harness file except this report (constraint honored; `git status` shows exactly the three additions).
## 1. `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` (438 lines)
Self-contained bash installer for the VLESS+REALITY endpoint on the user's Ubuntu/Debian VM. `set -euo pipefail`; `[setup]`-prefixed log/warn/die.

- **Argument validation FIRST (unprivileged, no network):** DOMAIN required and DNS-charset-checked (letters/digits/dots/hyphens, no leading/trailing dot or hyphen, at least one dot — also blocks JSON/CLI injection through the heredocs); PORT numeric 1-65535; DEST `host:port` or `[v6]:port` with port range check; INSTALL_ROOT absolute and whitespace-free (it is baked into the systemd ExecStart line); FORCE 0/1; stray positional args rejected; `-h/--help` prints usage. Then: root check (`id -u`), systemctl presence, deps check (curl/unzip/openssl — dies with the exact `apt-get update && apt-get install -y ...` command). - **Latest release, never hardcoded:** GitHub API `releases/latest` → `sed` parse of `tag_name` (validated `^v[0-9]...`), with a documented fallback to the `releases/latest` redirect (`url_effective`) because the unauthenticated API is per-IP rate-limited — this mattered in the sandbox itself (the API returned 403 rate-limit while the redirect still resolved to v26.11.9). - **Download → verify → install (no curl|bash):** zip to `mktemp -d` (0700, trap-cleanup on EXIT), `unzip -t` integrity check, extract xray/geoip.dat/geosite.dat, `xray version` smoke test, stop a running xray service first (ETXTBSY), then `install -D` 0755 binary + 0644 geo assets into `$INSTALL_ROOT/bin` and `$INSTALL_ROOT/share/xray`.
## 2. `README.md` (17 KB)

What it is (both binaries), ASCII layering diagram (apps → WinINET proxy → loopback xray inbounds → VLESS+REALITY → VM systemd xray → freedom; net-merge wintun as the single routing layer), the key design rationale (mux OFF, loopback-only inbounds, fail-open proxy policy, op_lock lifecycle + emergency-stop exit path, stale-proxy self-heal, connect order, backoff numbers), server-setup pointer, config reference table (all 23 fields with defaults matching `config.rs`, plus the empty/0-fallback and exe-dir path conventions), CLI reference for doctor/generate/connect/version/help and the tray binary (menu items verified against `menu_plan`, raw-status dump path verified, first-run template behavior verified), build instructions (stable Rust, native MSVC, cargo-zigbuild cross), CI/release story (ci.yml matrix + windows-target clippy; release.yml test-then-build on tags, zip contents, fail_on_unmatched_files), security notes (0600 writes, no secrets logged, gitignored config, unsigned-binary SmartScreen, UAC/admin, fail-open), MIT + THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, harness pointer. Every CLI claim was verified by building and running the console binary (`version`, no-arg pointer error, `doctor` on a filled config, `generate` writing 0600 xray-client.json with mux off). No emoji anywhere.
## 3. `QUICKSTART.md` (7 KB)

Ten-minute path, ordered: (0) get the release zip, (1) run the server script + firewall checklist + copy the client block, (2) install net-merge + `net-merge tray`, (3) Xray-core windows-64 zip → `bin\xray.exe` **plus geoip.dat/geosite.dat into `bin\`** (needed: the generated client config routes `geoip:private` direct and xray finds geo assets next to its exe), (4) `copy config.example.json config.json` + paste block, (5) elevated `multitunnel doctor` all green (elevation-warn nuance documented), (6) `multitunnel-tray.exe` with the **bold SMOKE TEST warning** — first run on real Windows, with the seven checkpoints: icon appears, left-click opens menu, menu dismisses on outside click (KB135788 fix), Connect → `State: Connected`, explorer restart via `Taskkill /IM explorer.exe /f` + restart → icon comes back (TaskbarCreated recovery), Disconnect/Exit clean, (7) optional headless `multitunnel connect` with the Ctrl+C/proxy note. ProtonVPN chain note included (rotation orthogonal, client never notices).
## Verification

Script: `bash -n` clean; validation matrix run for real (no DOMAIN, bad PORT, bad DEST, DEST port 0, bad DOMAIN charset/no-dot/leading-dot, relative and whitespace INSTALL_ROOT, bad FORCE, stray args, `--help`) — all clean `[setup] ERROR:` + exit 1; valid boundaries (mid-hyphen domain, PORT 1 and 65535, `[::1]:443` DEST, uppercase DOMAIN, FORCE=0) reach the root check, which correctly fails in the unprivileged sandbox; `xray x25519`/`uuid` parse, tag parse (compact + spaced JSON samples + live redirect), zip download/integrity/extract, `xray run -test` on the generated config, and the rendered client block were all exercised against the REAL v26.11.9 release artifacts (then cleaned from /tmp).

Gates (docs-only change, but rules are rules): `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (host), `cargo clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` **78/78**, `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (both PEs re-confirmed PE32+ console + GUI). No source file touched.
## Known residuals (for reviewers)

- `multitunnel` (console) with no command still prints the S3-era message "tray lands in stage S3 — build multitunnel-tray"; the README describes the actual behavior (a pointer to the GUI binary) without quoting the stale wording. Fixing the string would touch frozen `src/main.rs` — left for the orchestrator to arbitrate. - Public-IP detection prefers the GCP metadata server over api.ipify.org (spec listed ipify as the source): on this user's VM the egress may be ProtonVPN-routed, in which case ipify reports the VPN exit IP and the client block would be wrong. ipify remains the network fallback, with a warning when it is the source. - The gcloud "check first" step prints a plain `gcloud compute firewall-rules list` rather than an invented filter expression (unverifiable here, no gcloud in sandbox).

passages.text: # S4 Reviewer-B Report — SHIP / RELEASE-READINESS AUDIT (build / release / portability / licensing)

- Stage: S4 adversarial review, Reviewer-B. Stage S4 = Ship: `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` + `README.md` + `QUICKSTART.md` (commit 56340a5). This is the last gate before tagging **v0.1.0**. - Repo: /home/z/my-project/MultiTunnel, branch main, HEAD **56340a5**, working tree clean. S4 diff: exactly the 4 new files (+1027 lines) — no src/, .github/, Cargo.*, config.example.json change (verified: `git diff 06ad6aa..56340a5 -- Cargo.toml Cargo.lock .github/` is empty). - Context verified: the S3 review round closed with my P1 (message-only window) fixed at 799f6cd — hidden TOP-LEVEL `WS_OVERLAPPED` window, checked `SetForegroundWindow` return, `TaskbarCreated` re-registration (REV-C P1), `Supervisor::emergency_stop` + the 78th test (op-lock-free exit teardown).
## 1. Verification log (all run by me on 56340a5)

| Command | Result | |---|---| | `cargo test` | **78/78 ok**, 5.95 s, 0 ignored (config 9, core_proc 7, elevate 4, netmerge 16, supervisor 11, sysproxy 6, tray 20, xrayconf 5) | | `cargo fmt --check` | clean | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` (forced rebuild) | clean | | `cargo clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` | **clean** — full windows cfg surface (incl. tray FFI) type-checked | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (debug) | green | | `cargo zigbuild --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **green** (1m23s) — release-profile cross build, the closest local analog of the release job | | `file …/debug/*.exe` and `…/release/*.exe` | `multitunnel.exe` **PE32+ console**, `multitunnel-tray.exe` **PE32+ GUI** in BOTH profiles (release: 3.20 MB / 3.18 MB) | | `git show 56340a5 --stat` | QUICKSTART.md 153+, README.md 291+, s4-implementation.md, server/setup-xray-reality.sh 437+ — docs+script only | | `bash -n server/setup-xray-reality.sh` | clean; script is 0755 in-tree | | link liveness | github.com/net-merge/net-merge → 200; github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/releases → 200 (maintained upstreams, links in QUICKSTART accurate).
## 2. Release-readiness audit

### 2.1 release.yml trace — tag `v0.1.0` pushed hypothetically NOW windows-latest → checkout (Cargo.lock committed → reproducible deps) → stable toolchain → **`cargo test`** (65 tests on MSVC, see 2.7) → `cargo build --release` (both bins at `target/release/`, default target dir on the runner — paths in the Copy-Item match) → package: unconditional copy of `multitunnel.exe`, `multitunnel-tray.exe`, `config.example.json`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (all exist — a missing one would fail the step loudly, which is the desired behavior), guarded copy of `README.md` + `QUICKSTART.md` (both exist → included) → `Compress-Archive` → `dist/multitunnel-v0.1.0-windows-x64.zip` → upload-artifact → softprops release attach with `fail_on_unmatched_files: true` (the glob will match). **No missing path, no silent-degradation path: the release would build, test, package and attach successfully.** One content gap → P1-3 (server script not in the zip).

### 2.2 ci.yml on the tag push — is release-only testing enough? ci.yml does not run on tags (`branches: [main]`); release.yml carries `cargo test`. fmt/clippy are NOT run on the tag. Judgment: **acceptable** — in this project's flow every main push is CI-green (test on both OSes + lint + cross-check incl. windows-target clippy), and tags are cut from main HEAD; the release job re-runs the full suite on the exact tag commit, so the artifact is always *tested*. The residual (a tag of a never-pushed commit ships unlinted code) is a lint-regression risk, not a functional one → P2-1 optional belt-and-braces.

### 2.3 The zip a Windows user downloads Contents: `multitunnel.exe`, `multitunnel-tray.exe`, `config.example.json`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `README.md`, `QUICKSTART.md`. Client-side self-sufficient: QUICKSTART step 3 links XTLS/Xray-core releases (`Xray-windows-64.zip` — correct asset name; contains `xray.exe`, `geoip.dat`, `geosite.dat`; both maintained upstreams, no unmaintained sources) and step 2 links net-merge (live repo). The `bin\xray.exe` default matches `paths.xray` resolution (exe-dir-relative), and the geo-dat-next-to-exe note matches xray's asset lookup. **Gap: QUICKSTART step 1's server script is NOT in the zip** — a zip-only user must fetch the repo (no direct raw URL is given) → P1-3. Trivial nit: step 0 lists five items, the zip actually also carries README/QUICKSTART (P2-3).

### 2.4 MSVC-vs-gnu parity (shipped = MSVC, local proof = gnu) Risk judged **low**: windows-sys 0.61.2 and winreg are the same crate versions with identical FFI declarations for both ABIs (win32 is a stable C ABI; windows-link import shims are toolchain-agnostic); the gnu side is proven by zigbuild (debug + release) + clippy `-D warnings` + PE import inspection; the MSVC side compiles and runs 65 tests in CI. Rust MSVC release binaries carry the CRT statically (no vcruntime DLL prerequisite). No printf/CRT-dependent behavior exists in the code paths. The genuinely untested-until-now part — the tray UI at runtime — is exactly what QUICKSTART step 6 turns into the documented first-run smoke test (with 7 checkpoints and a "report it" escape hatch). Acceptable for v0.1.0 with that backstop.

### 2.5 Licensing chain for the release artifact - Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock byte-identical since S2-close → the S2-round-2-verified THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (all 19 dep crates, permissive MIT / MIT-OR-Apache-2.0 / MIT-OR-Unlicense; full MIT text) is still current. **Zero new dependencies in S3/S4.** - The zip redistributes only project code (MIT) + statically-linked permissive crates + docs. Xray-core (MPL-2.0) and net-merge (MIT) are downloaded by the user from their own upstreams (QUICKSTART links; server script downloads from XTLS releases) — never bundled → **no copyleft contamination**. The setup script similarly downloads rather than embeds. - The tray icon is original generated artwork (project's own committed script) → project MIT. No third-party assets. - SmartScreen/unsigned-binary warning: covered in README (Security notes) and QUICKSTART step 6.1. UAC/admin expectations documented in both.

### 2.6 Docs build claims `cargo build --release` produces both binaries (proven locally in the release profile via zigbuild); the zigbuild cross instructions match the exact commands this harness runs; MSRV 1.78 matches Cargo.toml (verified exact in S2 r2: code max 1.70, deps ≤1.71, lockfile v4 ⇒ 1.78); "Linux build compiles stubs" is true; CI description matches the actual workflows (test matrix, lint, cross-check incl. windows-target clippy); harness pointer present. Version: Cargo.toml `0.1.0` ↔ planned tag `v0.1.0` ↔ zip name `multitunnel-v0.1.0-windows-x64.zip` — consistent. **Two doc-accuracy defects → P1-1 (restartMax semantics), P1-2 (stale S3 string vs README description).**

### 2.7 Windows-leg test count and safety Host runs 78. `#[cfg(unix)]`-gated tests (exhaustively enumerated by multiline grep): supervisor 6 (op-lock wait, emergency stop, 4 rig tests), core_proc 2 (start-twice, drip deadline), netmerge 7 (process tests) = **15 excluded**; `#[cfg(windows)]`-only sysproxy tests: 2 (mapping helpers). **Windows leg = 78 − 15 + 2 = 65.** Safety: all 65 are pure / temp-dir file IO / loopback binds; the two loopback-binding core_proc stub tests carry the S2-round-2 `set_nonblocking(false)` hardening; every timing-sensitive test (drip 350–900 ms window, op-lock 300 ms, start-twice <1 s, emergency-stop <2 s, core-death 15 s deadline, 20 s recv bounds) is unix-gated, so the Windows leg carries no timing risk. Windows runners handle temp dirs, loopback binds, and the file-IO dump tests without issue (same tests have been green on the windows-latest CI leg since S2). **Low risk of a Windows-leg failure at tag time.**

### 2.8 Server script (portability/lens notes; deep security is REV-C's) `set -euo pipefail`; validation-before-root; no curl|bash (download → `unzip -t` → extract → smoke test → `install -D`); mktemp 0700 with EXIT trap; ETXTBSY handled (stop service before replacing binary); `xray run -test` gate on the generated config; both `xray x25519` output generations parsed; JSON built from charset-validated variables (no injection through DOMAIN/DEST/keys); GitHub-API rate-limit fallback to the `releases/latest` redirect (verified live: this sandbox's IP is currently rate-limited on api.github.com — the fallback path is real-world exercised); pipefail/SIGPIPE analyzed for every `sed | head` pipeline (each sed emits at most one line → no SIGPIPE-141 under `set -e`). GNU-isms (`sed s///I`, `install -D`) are unreachable on non-systemd hosts (earlier clean die "targets Ubuntu/Debian"). Config written 0644 root:root because `User=nobody` must read it → P2-2 (0640 root:nogroup would be tighter). systemd unit hardening (NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict/ProtectHome/PrivateTmp) as documented in README.
## 3. Findings by severity

### P0 — none The tagged release would not fail: every workflow path exists, both exes build and test green on the exact commands CI uses (host + windows-gnu + release profile), licensing is clean, the zip is complete for the client side, and the Windows CI leg carries no identified failure risk.

**P1-1. README config table inverts `restartMax` semantics — ships in the zip.** README.md:153 — "`behavior.restartMax` | 5 | core restart budget after failures **(0 = unlimited)**". Actual behavior: `restart_campaign` (supervisor.rs) treats `max == 0` as *give up immediately — never restart* (the S2 contract: "restart_max (0 = never)"), and `apply_fallback_defaults` (config.rs:174-212) deliberately does NOT 0-fallback `restartMax`, so a JSON `0` reaches the supervisor as "never". Also the blanket claim at README.md:155-156 ("numbers set to `0` fall back to these defaults on load") is false for this one field. A user setting `restartMax: 0` expecting unlimited retries gets a fail-fast tunnel that disables the system proxy on the first core death. Fix the table line to "0 = never restart (fail immediately)" and scope the 0-fallback sentence.

**P1-2. Stale stage-3 string in the shipped console binary contradicts the README.** `multitunnel` with no args prints `error: tray lands in stage S3 — build multitunnel-tray` and exits 1 (verified against the built binary). README.md:170 documents "(none) print a pointer to multitunnel-tray (the tray app is the GUI binary)". In v0.1.0, "stage S3" is meaningless jargon for an end user and the wording/behavior doesn't match the docs that ship next to it. One-string fix in `src/main.rs:49-51` (frozen file — the implementer flagged it for orchestrator arbitration; as release reviewer I escalate: fix before tagging).

**P1-3. The release zip lacks `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` — QUICKSTART step 1's prerequisite.** release.yml:23 copies exes + config.example.json + LICENSE + notices (+ guarded README/QUICKSTART). QUICKSTART step 1 tells the user to "copy `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` there (or fetch the repo)" — a zip-only user has no script and no direct URL. One line (`Copy-Item server/setup-xray-reality.sh` after creating the dir, or adding `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` to the unconditional list) makes the zip self-sufficient for the whole 10-minute path; alternatively add the raw-GitHub URL to QUICKSTART step 1. Fix before tagging (re-tagging after the fact is worse than one more line now).

**P2-1. release.yml runs `cargo test` but no fmt/clippy on the tag.** Acceptable today (tags cut from CI-green main; the artifact is fully tested), but adding the two lint steps to the release job (~4 lines) closes the "tag of an untested commit ships unlinted" residual permanently.

**P2-2. Server config file is world-readable (0644 root:root) and holds the REALITY private key.** Deliberate (the service runs as `User=nobody` and must read it; documented), but `install -m 0640 -o root -g nogroup` (Ubuntu's nobody group) is tighter while staying service-readable. Note: `nobody`'s group is `nogroup` on Debian/Ubuntu — worth a quick verification on the target VM before switching.

**P2-3. QUICKSTART step 0 under-lists the zip contents** (5 items; README.md and QUICKSTART.md are also inside). Trivial; also consider mentioning that extracting yields a `multitunnel-v0.1.0` folder (Compress-Archive keeps the directory) so users know what "extract into C:\Tools\MultiTunnel" produces.
## 4. Verdict

**APPROVE** — 0 P0. The release pipeline is mechanically sound end-to-end (verified path-by-path, plus a local release-profile cross build as the closest analog of the runner's build), licensing is clean with zero dependency drift since the audited S2 state, and the Windows CI leg (65 tests) carries no identified failure risk. The three P1s are documentation/shipping-completeness fixes that do not affect whether the release builds and attaches — but all three ship user-visible wrongness in v0.1.0 (an inverted config-table claim, stale stage jargon in the binary, and a missing step-1 prerequisite in the zip), and each is a one-to-three-line fix. **Recommendation: apply the three P1s, re-run the gates, then tag.**
