passages.text: # S4 Review — Reviewer-C (Correctness & Security; server script + docs)

- **Reviewer:** Reviewer-C, adversarial round, stage S4 (Ship) - **Date:** 2026-11-13, repo HEAD `56340a5` (S4 = `56340a5` on base `06ad6aa`), branch main, clean tree — no files modified; only this report written. - **Scope:** `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` audited as hostile root-running software; `README.md` + `QUICKSTART.md` cross-checked line-by-line against `src/main.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/tray.rs`, `config.example.json`, `.github/workflows/*`; implementer claims re-proven where possible.
## Verification log (run myself, trusted nothing)

| Gate | Result | |---|---| | `cargo test` | **78/78 passed, 0 failed** in 5.95 s (77 at S3 close + 1 from the S3 P1 fixes) | | `cargo clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` | **clean** — exit 0 | | `bash -n server/setup-xray-reality.sh` | **clean** | | `git show 56340a5 --stat` | exactly 4 new files (script, README, QUICKSTART, impl.
## Script audit (root-running software standard)

**`set -euo pipefail` discipline — holds.** Every expansion is double-quoted; all interpolations into heredocs are charset-validated before use (DOMAIN `[A-Za-z0-9.-]` with edge rules, PORT all-digits + range, DEST regex `host:port`/`[v6]:port` + port range, INSTALL_ROOT absolute + whitespace-free, keys `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`, shortId/uuid generator-produced) → **no JSON or ExecStart injection is possible** (re-proven with a `a".evil` DOMAIN attempt). The three `cmd | head -n 1` pipelines either output ≤1 line (no SIGPIPE possible under pipefail) or are `|| true`-guarded (`xray version | head`); command-substitution failures land in `TAG`-empty → guarded die. `WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"` + `chmod 0700` + `trap cleanup EXIT` → temp dir always removed.

**No curl|sh; download failure handled.** Zip → temp file → `-s` empty check → `unzip -t` integrity → extract exactly `xray geoip.dat geosite.dat` → per-file existence checks → `chmod 0755` → `xray version` smoke test (catches wrong architecture loudly) → `install -D` into `$INSTALL_ROOT`. `curl -fSL --retry 3 … || die` on the download. The GitHub-API rate-limit case degrades to the `releases/latest` redirect, and both paths terminate in the `^v[0-9]…` tag guard — re-proven above.

**Credentials.** `xray uuid`; `xray x25519` parsed for BOTH output generations (re-proven above); `openssl rand -hex 8` shortId (64 bits — adequate for REALITY's anti-probe salt). The private key is never printed (client block carries `publicKey` only; the `log` line prints uuid/shortId which are client-side values anyway) and never leaves the VM.

**REALITY config validity.** Field set (`show:false, dest, xver:0, serverNames, privateKey, shortIds`) is the current documented shape; `dest` (not the legacy `target` spelling) is what current Xray accepts; VLESS `decryption:"none"` + client `flow:"xtls-rprx-vision"` correct; and the script hard-fails via `xray run -test` **before** touching the service if anything is wrong. Existing config + no FORCE → refusal with regeneration warning (no silent credential rotation). (Implementer's real-binary `-test` pass is credible; tooling no longer present here — noted, not re-run.)

**systemd unit.** Sound for Ubuntu 22.04+: `User=nobody` + `Environment=XRAY_LOCATION_ASSET=$ASSET_DIR` (assets 0644 in 0755 dirs — readable), `ExecStart` path from whitespace-validated INSTALL_ROOT (systemd takes it verbatim — no shell, so no metachar risk), `Restart=always`+`RestartSec=3`, `NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict/ProtectHome/PrivateTmp` (xray needs no writes outside stdout → journald). `daemon-reload` → `enable` (guarded) → `restart` → `sleep 2` → `is-active --quiet`; on failure dumps 30 journal lines and dies naming the state — a crash-looping service reads as not-active, so the check cannot pass a broken endpoint. A bind failure (e.g. port taken) exits xray → crash-loop → caught. Good.

**Firewall guidance.** Non-destructive: `iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport $PORT -j ACCEPT` (insert, **no `-F` anywhere in the repo**) + `netfilter-persistent save`; explicit "check existing rules first" steps; the gcloud command is syntactically correct with a narrower-source-ranges suggestion. Print-only (script never touches the firewall itself) — correct choice.

**Public IP.** GCP metadata (correct endpoint + `Metadata-Flavor` header, IPv4-validated) preferred over ipify with an explicit VPN-egress warning on the ipify path; placeholder + guidance when neither works. Sound; the metadata preference is the right call for a VM whose egress may be VPN-routed.
**Gaps found** → findings P1-1/P2-1/2/3 below (teardown-on-failure story, config mode, privileged-port validation).
## Docs cross-check (README/QUICKSTART vs code)

Verified accurate: architecture diagram & design contracts (mux off, loopback-only, geoip:private direct, fail-open, op_lock + emergency_stop, stale-proxy self-heal, connect order, backoff 1→30 s) — all match lib.rs/supervisor.rs/xrayconf.rs; doctor check list & order (QUICKSTART step 5 = main.rs exactly, incl. "all checks passed"); `generate` 0600; `connect` UAC/elevation/summary/Ctrl+C semantics; tray menu items, `State:` wording, Links line variants, `state\net-merge-status.txt` dump path, 1 s tooltip, TaskbarCreated re-registration and the emergency-teardown Exit — **both S3 P1 features exist in code** (`RegisterWindowMessageW` re-add, `Supervisor::emergency_stop` after the 2 s exit bound) so the QUICKSTART smoke-test checkpoints are truthful; release.yml description (test-first, zip contents, `fail_on_unmatched_files`); .gitignore really contains `config.json` (+ `xray-client.json`, `*.exe`, logs/state/bin); MSRV 1.78; **smoke-test warning present and prominent**; **no emoji** (programmatic scan); all 23 config-table defaults match `config.rs` **except the restartMax semantics and server.address fallback noted below**; geoip.dat/geosite.dat instruction in QUICKSTART step 3 is **genuinely required** (the generated client config's `geoip:private` routing rule fails xray startup without geoip.dat; xray finds assets next to its exe; the server script mirrors the same convention).
Inaccurate (findings): `restartMax (0 = unlimited)`, net-merge "on your PATH", `server.address` default/fallback, and the CI push-trigger claim — details below.
## Findings

### P0 — 0 The script is careful root-running software: injection-proof, download-verified, loudly-failing, secret-preserving; nothing that breaks a VM, installs a broken endpoint, or opens a security hole. (The `-test`-before-restart gate in particular means a bad generated config can never take the endpoint down.)

### P1 — 4 1. **`README.md:153`** — "`behavior.restartMax` … (0 = unlimited)" is **factually wrong**: per the supervisor contract and `restart_campaign` (`if max == 0 || attempt > max` → give up), **0 = never restart** (immediate give-up, proxy restored, `Failed`). A user following the README to get "unlimited" resilience gets zero. One-word doc fix. 2. **`QUICKSTART.md:47`** — "Make sure `net-merge` is on your PATH **or** sits next to `multitunnel.exe`": with the default config (`"netMerge": "net-merge"`), `config.rs::resolve` joins the relative name onto the **executable's directory**, and a directory-qualified program is not PATH-searched — so a PATH-only install fails `doctor`/bonding (empirically re-proven: relative paths resolve against the exe dir in my doctor run). Only "next to the exe" (or an absolute `paths.netMerge`) works; the sentence's first disjunct misleads users into a broken step 2. 3. **`README.md:134` + `:155`** — the config table lists `server.address` with default `35.208.99.240`, and the conventions paragraph claims "strings left empty … fall back to these defaults on load". **False for `server.address`**: it has no load-time fallback (only `server.port` and the local/paths/behavior fields do); an empty address is rejected by `validate()` (empirically re-proven: `doctor -config` → "incomplete config — missing: server.address"). The 35.208.99.240 value is a template/example prefill; the table should mark address required like uuid/sni/publicKey, and the convention sentence should be scoped. 4.

### P2 — 6 1. `server/setup-xray-reality.sh:214-337` — no failure-rollback: after `systemctl stop xray` (upgrade path), any failure before `systemctl restart` (install/credential/validation/unit error) leaves the old endpoint STOPPED with no restart attempt and only a raw `set -e` exit (`install`/`chmod`/`chown`/`systemctl restart` have no `|| die` diagnostics); the subsequent re-run then demands `FORCE=1`, which regenerates all credentials (killing the old client block) even though the old config is still valid. Suggest a failure trap that best-effort `systemctl start xray`, plus a "config unchanged — `systemctl start xray` recovers" hint. 2. `server/setup-xray-reality.sh:297` — config written `0644 root:root`; `chown root:nogroup` + `chmod 0640` would keep it readable by `User=nobody` (nobody's group is nogroup on Debian/Ubuntu) while hiding the REALITY private key from other local users; also create under `umask 077` to close the pre-chmod window. The implementer's "local read = already on the box" argument is acceptable for a dedicated VM — noted as defense-in-depth, not a blocker. 3. `server/setup-xray-reality.sh:95-100` — PORT < 1024 (e.g. `PORT=443`, or `PORT=08` → 8) passes validation but `User=nobody` cannot bind privileged ports → the service fails at start (caught loudly by is-active, but with a cryptic journal). Pre-validate `PORT ≥ 1024` or warn. 4. `README.md:170` — "(none) print a pointer to multitunnel-tray" describes intent; the actual no-arg behavior prints the stale S3-era string "tray lands in stage S3 — build multitunnel-tray" and exits FAILURE.

### Deviation judgments requested - **geoip/geosite in QUICKSTART**: justified — the generated client config's `geoip:private` routing rule hard-requires geoip.dat at xray startup; geosite.dat is not strictly needed (no geosite rules) but ships in the same zip and costs nothing to copy. The "next to the executable" location is where xray looks absent `XRAY_LOCATION_ASSET` (the supervisor sets none). - **Config 0644 root-owned**: acceptable for a single-user VM per the implementer's argument, with the 0640 root:nogroup improvement noted as P2-2. - **GCP-metadata-over-ipify**: correct deviation — on a VPN-egress VM, ipify reports the VPN exit IP and the client block would be wrong; metadata reports the true external IP; ipify remains the fallback with a warning. - **`xray run -test` verification**: not re-runnable here (tooling cleaned from /tmp); the script's built-in gate order (test config → die before touching the service) plus the implementer's real-binary validation record give adequate confidence.
## Verdict

**APPROVE.** No P0: the installer is injection-proof, verifies everything it downloads and generates, fails loudly rather than half-working, never prints the private key, and cannot replace a working endpoint with a broken config (the `-test` gate). The four P1s are documentation/CI accuracy issues — three false claims in the new docs (restartMax=0 semantics, net-merge PATH resolution, server.address fallback) and one pre-existing-but-now-documented CI trigger corruption (`branches: ain]`) — all one-to-few-line fixes that should land before the v0.1.0 tag, but none breaks a user's VM, ships a broken endpoint, or opens a security hole.
# S5-REV-B verdict: APPROVE

Reviewer lens: BUILD / PORTABILITY (windows-gnu vs msvc) / DEPENDENCY+LICENSE HYGIENE / TEST QUALITY / CI+DOCS ACCURACY. Scope reviewed: `git diff 07ef5c5..40ee65c` (14 files, +1716/−255) plus the full current state of every touched source file, both workflows, the server script, the docs, and independent runs of every gate.
No P0. No P1. Eight P2s (doc/robustness nits, all fixable at close or carried). All 19 contract items verified implemented and tested; all gates reproduce green.
## Findings
### P0 (blocks approval) — file:line + argument + suggested fix
None.
### P1 (should fix before release)

None rose to P1. The closest candidate (snapshot downgrade gap, P2-1 below) was downgraded: the common-case snapshot round-trips both directions, the failure mode is non-destructive (v0.1.0 refuses to guess rather than deleting data) and recoverable by deleting `state/sysproxy.json`.
### P2 (nits)

1. **Snapshot downgrade direction undocumented** — `src/sysproxy.rs:52-56` (`SnapValue` doc: "JSON shape (backward compatible with pre-S5 snapshots)") and `src/sysproxy.rs:218-227`. The claim is true for the direction it states (v0.1.0 file → v0.2.0 binary; verified: the legacy test at `src/sysproxy.rs:611` pins the *actual* v0.1.0 on-disk shape — `proxyEnable` always a plain number, strings `null`/string, per `git show 07ef5c5:src/sysproxy.rs` — not a hand-invented format). The reverse direction is only partially compatible: a v0.2.0-written snapshot containing `"proxyEnable": null` (Absent — new shape; v0.1.0 always wrote a number) or any `{"opaqueKind": …}` marker fails v0.1.0's `u32`/`Option<String>` parse (`#[serde(default)]` does not rescue a present-but-wrong-typed field), so a downgraded v0.1.0 `load_snapshot` errs → `restore` errs → the stale snapshot persists and the proxy stays set until the file is deleted. Narrow (requires downgrade while a snapshot exists AND ProxyEnable absent/Opaque) and recoverable. Suggested fix: one doc sentence on `Snapshot` noting the downgrade caveat ("v0.2.0 snapshots containing `null`/`opaqueKind` markers will not parse on v0.1.0 — delete state/sysproxy.json after downgrade"); optionally serialize DWORD `Absent` as `0` (semantically identical: `EnableAction::Write(0)`) to keep even that corner downgrade-readable. No code change required for approval.

2. **rust-cache on the release tag is effectively a cold cache** — `.github/workflows/release.yml:17`. rust-cache's default key includes the workflow name ("release" ≠ "ci"), and GitHub cache scoping means caches saved on a tag ref are not restorable by later tags (only default-branch caches are). Harmless (perf only); the cache step still satisfies contract D2 as written ("default key + the workflow name"). Optional: `prefix-key` shared with ci.yml, or drop the step from release.yml.

1. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:336` — leftover debug `eprintln!` in the production liveness path.** `child_addr_if_alive()` — called on EVERY engine connect/probe (i.e. per proxied connection) — contains `eprintln!("[dbg-eng] probe pid={pid:?} tw={tw:?}")` in non-test code. Byte-verified with `od -An -c` (sandbox output-filter rule). This violates global contract rule 5 ("tracing for diagnostics, no println! in libs") and will spam stderr of `multitunnel gui` with one line per tunnel connection. It leaks no credentials (pid + try_wait result only) but is exactly the class of leftover that must not ship. One-line deletion.

2. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:450-461` — the v0.2 kill-on-close Job Object was not ported; `xray.exe` is orphaned on abnormal GUI death.** The module doc claims "the exact `core_proc` discipline", but `src/core_proc.rs:583-618` (added by the 2026-11-17 v0.2-audit REV-C#2 backport, commit ff0abb4) puts the child in a Windows Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` so the *kernel* guarantees "the core cannot outlive this process". `ManagedEngine` relies solely on `Drop::kill_current()`, which does not run on `TerminateProcess` (Task Manager kill), console Ctrl+C (the C-runtime exits without unwinding), power loss, or panic-abort — the precise scenarios the v0.2 audit fixed. Normal window close is safe (runtime drop cancels tasks → Arc chain → Drop → kill), so the orphan trigger is abnormal death; the orphan then runs an open REALITY tunnel with a loopback listener indefinitely. Restore the job-object wrapper (cfg(windows)) around the spawned child, or route spawns through `core_proc`.

3. **`src/real_service.rs:919-949,688-714` + `crates/mt-app/src/app.rs:831-842` + `src/main.rs:605-625` — the GUI path loses the S2 supervisor's fail-open/self-heal contract for the system proxy (D5).** Three facets, one root cause (RealService has no supervision loop and no lifecycle hook): **(a)** closing the GUI window while Connected (or Ctrl+C on the console host) never calls `disconnect()`/`sysproxy::restore` — no `window::close` subscription, no exit hook in `cmd_gui`; the registry keeps pointing at the now-dead `127.0.0.1:10809`. **(b)** Nothing heals a stale snapshot at startup: v0.2 `connect` step 0 is "sysproxy::restore() best-effort" (supervisor.rs:25, contract line); `RealService::connect_flow` has no equivalent, and `disconnect()` in a fresh instance is a no-op (`sysproxy_set=false`), so a crashed run leaves browsing blackholed until the user manually fixes Windows settings or completes a full connect→disconnect cycle. **(c)** Engine give-up does not restore: after `ManagedEngine` exhausts its respawn budget the outbound errors permanently while `RealService` state stays `Connected` and the system proxy stays set — the v0.2 supervisor restored the proxy on restart exhaustion (supervisor.rs:20-22, D5). Keep-first `save_snapshot` (sysproxy.rs:219-223) does protect the user's original values from being overwritten, so this is recoverable-but-stuck, not data loss. Distinct from the parked "no-snapshot-disable UX" backlog item: v0.2 had all three recovery paths; v0.3's GUI has none.

4. **`src/real_service.rs:696-699,587-588` — LAN/private traffic no longer bypasses the tunnel when the GUI system proxy is on (regression of a stated top-3 design principle).** `lib.rs:22` lists "LAN/private traffic bypasses the tunnel" as a project invariant, implemented in v0.2 twice over: the proxy override default is the full LAN bypass list `localhost;127.*;10.*;192.168.*;…;<local>` (config.rs:134-139) AND the generated Xray config routes `geoip:private → direct` (xrayconf.rs:66). The S6 RealService path writes a hard-coded `ProxyOverride="localhost"` only, and the `Router` starts with an empty rule list whose default action is `Proxy` (SettingsFile default rules = `Vec::new()`). Net effect with `system_proxy=true`: requests to 192.168.x/10.x/172.16-31.x (router admin pages, printers, NAS) are sent through the VLESS tunnel to the remote server — breaking local access and leaking LAN hostnames/IPs to the tunnel operator. Fix: seed the default rules with a private-CIDR → direct rule (or route private IPs direct in `ProxyServer::establish`) and write the v0.2 LAN bypass override.

5. **`crates/mt-platform/src/engine.rs:129-133` (via `crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:412`) — engine-download errors echo the full request URL, which can carry a credential (D9).** `ReqwestFetch::fetch` propagates `reqwest::Error` via `?`; its `Display` includes the full URL ("error sending request for url (…)"). The chain `ensure() → "engine \`{tag}\`: binary download failed: {e}" → connect error string → GUI LogLine + tracing` therefore prints whatever `$MULTITUNNEL_ENGINE_URL` contains — and user-set download-mirror URLs with embedded tokens (`https://host/xray.zip?token=…`) are a common pattern; the token then persists in GUI logs and any pasted bug report. mt-links solved exactly this with `reqwest::Error::without_url()` (subscription.rs:100-108) — mt-platform needs the same treatment in `fetch` (and `error_for_status` on the same line).

1. **`src/real_service.rs:661,932-934` — stale `disconnect_requested` flag can spuriously abort one later connect.** A `disconnect()` landing in the window between the post-probe flag check (line 661) and session installation sets the flag but leaves the session Connected; the flag is consumed only by a later `connect_flow`, which then aborts itself right after its probe (one lost connect click, self-healing thereafter). Clear the flag at `begin_connect` or after session install. The service already implements cancellation (`disconnect_requested` honored after the probe) — the GUI just never calls it in that state. NEW. 3. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:316-324,428-430` + `src/real_service.rs:1015-1020` — two engines with the same profile tag race on shared files.** `test_latency` on the active profile while connected builds a second `ManagedEngine` with the same tag; both write `engine-<tag>.tmp` → `engine-<tag>.json` (one can truncate the other's in-flight temp; the fsutil single-writer assumption from S5-REV-C P2-6 is now reachable) and append to the same log handle. ## Verdict rationale

The S6 expert crates are individually solid: parsers are panic-free and credential-redacted, the data plane matches its frozen contract in every detail I could pin down, the zip installer's zip-slip and atomicity story is sound, and all six gates pass with a 321-test suite. What keeps this at five P1s rather than a BLOCK is that none of them is an exploitable hole, credential *value* leak to a remote party, data loss, or a reachable panic/deadlock — the closest to the P0 bar are the D5 fail-open regression (P1-3) and the LAN-bypass regression (P1-4), both of which require the user to enable the system-proxy feature and both recoverable by manual action. But they are real regressions against deliberately-fixed guarantees (the v0.2-audit Job Object, the S2 stale-heal/give-up contract, the "LAN bypasses the tunnel" invariant), and P1-1/P1-5 are trivial fixes, so all five should land before the v0.3 release ships. APPROVE per D6 (zero P0s), with the P1 list as the release blocker checklist.
